title: How to Avoid the Top 5 Phone Scams Targeting Seniors in 2026
bigPicture: Learn the common signs of phone scams and simple steps to stay safe.
whatYouNeedToKnow: Scammers pretend to be from trusted groups like the government, your bank, or a charity.
They create urgency, saying you must act now or you will lose money or benefits.
They often ask for personal info, money, or gift cards to solve a fake problem.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Giving out your Social Security number, bank account, or credit card details over the phone.
Sending money with gift cards, wire transfers, or cryptocurrency to someone you do not know.
actionSteps: Hang up right away if the caller pressures you or asks for money or personal info.
Call back using a phone number you know is real, like the one on your bill or the official website.
Never share passwords, PINs, or account numbers unless you made the call.
Write down the caller’s number and what they said, then tell a trusted friend or family member.
Report the call to the FTC at reportfraud.ftc.gov or to your local police.
